mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter indicates strong economic growth, which is typically associated with higher corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the quarters where GDPC1 increased by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month suggests an improving labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last two months indicates a robust supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it reflects increased economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is often associated with a broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 5% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it suggests inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in the last month indicates strong consumer spending, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it reflects robust economic demand.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% in the last month.
